propositions.statement: Lutar-Readiness Monotonicity: R(Lambda, ASL) is non-increasing in ASL for any fixed Lambda-vector. Raising ASL from level k to k+1 either holds R constant (if new required thresholds already met) or strictly decreases R (if any newly tightened threshold is not met).
propositions.proof_sketch: By inspection of required coverage map in spec §4.3: only doctrineAlignment threshold changes with ASL (rises from 0.90 to 0.95 at ASL>=3). If lambdaScores.doctrineAlignment in [0.90, 0.95) when ASL jumps to 3, axis drops from passing set, reducing coverage/9 by 1/9 ~= 0.11. No threshold change can add a previously failing axis to passing set, so R cannot increase with ASL.
propositions.operational_implication: ASL escalation is a HALT-eligible event by construction. Gate 4 cannot be bypassed by holding Lambda-vector constant while escalating autonomy.

propositions.statement: Brier Score as Calibration Lower Bound: B_agg >= ECE^2, where B_agg is aggregate Brier score over n settled predictions and ECE is expected-calibration-error of the same prediction set.
propositions.proof_sketch: From Murphy (1973) decomposition: B = REL - RES + UNC. Reliability REL is mean squared calibration error over probability bins, which dominates ECE^2 in expectation over uniform bin widths (DeGroot & Fienberg 1983). Hence rising B_agg implies rising ECE, making B_agg a conservative (lower-bound) proxy for calibration degradation.
propositions.connection_to_th8: When TH8b (grade-1 receipt determinism) is proved in Lean, deterministic receipts will have B_agg=0 by construction: a deterministic agent always outputs the same value for the same input => zero forecast error on its own outputs => ECE <= sqrt(B_agg) = 0.
